subject.title: fix(channels): recover stale ingress queue claims at gateway startup

question: Should OpenClaw accept an age-based gateway-startup sweep for stale SQLite ingress claims, and how should its restart skip gates be reconciled with current main's SQLite restart-handoff implementation?
rationale: The fix addresses a real P1 message-delivery deadlock, but it intentionally mutates persisted delivery state at startup and the branch conflicts with the current restart-handoff implementation.

options.title: Refresh And Land Startup Sweep
options.body: Rebase the branch, port the skip guard to current SQLite restart handoff, rerun focused queue/startup/restart validation, and keep this PR as the fix path.

options.title: Require Durable Lease Design
options.body: Ask for a heartbeat or claim-owner lease design instead of age-based startup recovery before accepting persisted-state mutation.

options.title: Pause This Branch
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers want the remaining work handled by a new branch after deciding the restart and lease boundary.

recommendation.title: Refresh And Land Startup Sweep
recommendation.body: Rebase the branch, port the skip guard to current SQLite restart handoff, rerun focused queue/startup/restart validation, and keep this PR as the fix path.

likelyOwner.reason: The central shared SQLite ingress queue storage path traces to this history, and the decision is about the core channel state boundary rather than Telegram-only code.
